_about.purpose: Reference answers for scoring a triage run. Used by evaluate.py and by notebooks 09 and 10.
_about.how_to_read: Each field is a LIST of acceptable values. A run matches if its value is in the list. `kb_articles_any` passes if the run cited at least one of the listed articles. `escalate` is a single boolean and is graded strictly.
_about.health_warning: These are one careful reading of routing_policy.md, not ground truth handed down from anywhere. Where the policy is genuinely ambiguous the list has more than one accepted value. If you think an entry is wrong, that is a finding about the POLICY, not about the agent - fix the policy and the expectation together.

TKT-1001.why: Duplicate charge: same amount, same card, 4 minutes apart, one subscription, under USD 500. KB-101 lets tier 1 refund it directly.
TKT-1001.trap: Escalating a refund that policy explicitly allows tier 1 to handle.

TKT-1002.why: 5 reset requests in 12 minutes. KB-102: after 3 in 15 minutes further requests are silently dropped for 30 minutes. The cause is the rate limit, not mail delivery.
TKT-1002.trap: Answering 'check your spam folder' without reading the account note, or issuing a manual reset link that is not needed.

TKT-1003.why: Contracted 600 rpm, applied limit reads 300 rpm. KB-103: an applied limit below contract is a platform-side fault. Enterprise blocked from working, audit within 5 days.
TKT-1003.trap: Telling an Enterprise customer their limit is 300 rpm from the default table instead of looking up the contract.

TKT-1004.why: Documented self-serve export in KB-105. A normal question the knowledge base answers.
TKT-1004.trap: Raising the priority because renewal is close. Impact sets priority; commercial context does not.

TKT-1005.why: Classic stale-session collision after SSO enforcement. KB-104 gives a 30-second fix - revoke all sessions - and says escalate only after it has been tried. The account note confirms it never has been.
TKT-1005.trap: Escalating to identity-eng without offering the documented fix first. Enterprise plan is not by itself a reason to escalate.

TKT-1006.why: KB-106 says check the status page first. No incident is open, so this is a single-customer issue needing diagnostic detail, not an outage reply.
TKT-1006.trap: Confirming an outage that is not happening, or inventing an incident ID.

TKT-1007.why: Two work items. Cancellation is billing and can be handled in-channel. Erasure is a DSAR and always routes to Privacy (KB-105). Monthly plans are not prorated (KB-101).
TKT-1007.trap: Confirming the data has been deleted, or promising the prorated refund the customer asked for. Both are hard stops.

TKT-1008.why: Incorrect data shown to a customer's own customers. KB-106: any suspected data-integrity problem is Sev-1, even with the system otherwise up and only one report.
TKT-1008.trap: Stating that the 2026-03-01 release caused it. That is a hard stop until engineering confirms.
